summary.text: Aaron Qin is the Greens candidate for Box Hill at the 2026 Victorian election. A registered nurse, he founded a small business that provides in-home care for older people, and he chairs the Australia Multicultural Care Support Association.

priorities.text: people here deserve practical leadership and better decisions

sources.title: Box Hill: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
Aaron Qin, Candidate for Box Hill, Australian Greens Victoria

summary.text: Heena Cheung is standing as an independent for Box Hill at the 2026 Victorian election. She works in public health as chief operating officer of an NDIS provider, founded a registered charity aimed at preventing child sexual abuse, and sits on Whitehorse City Council's multicultural advisory committee. She first came to Box Hill as a student in 2015, and her campaign centres on the Box Hill brickworks site, residents' say in planning decisions and funding for neighbourhood houses.

occupation.text: Public health professional; chief operating officer of an NDIS provider

prior_roles.role: Founder, not-for-profit working to prevent child sexual abuse
NGO delegate, 70th session of the UN Commission on the Status of Women

previous_candidacies.note: Wikipedia lists an ungrouped Senate candidate in Victoria with this name; neither her campaign site nor the ABC mentions it, so it may not be the same person.

priorities.text: Turning the heritage-listed Box Hill brickworks land into parkland instead of high-rise towers
A legal requirement for 90 days of binding community consultation on planning decisions
Closing the funding gap for Whitehorse's neighbourhood houses
Cost-of-living relief through stamp duty reform, an end to hidden school fees and an urgent care clinic
Support for Treaty, truth-telling and Aboriginal community-controlled organisations

sources.title: Box Hill: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
Heena4Boxhill: A Strong Voice. A Fairer Box Hill (campaign site)

summary.text: Jamie Baker is the One Nation candidate for Box Hill at the 2026 Victorian election. The ABC's guide says he grew up in the area and still lives there with his family, and that he has spent over 30 years in construction and operates a registered building business.

occupation.text: Builder; runs a registered building company

sources.title: Box Hill: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News

summary.text: Paul Hamer won Box Hill for Labor in 2018 and has held it since. He joined cabinet in April 2026 and has been Minister for Roads and Road Safety since August 2026. He is recontesting Box Hill in 2026.

prior_roles.role: Minister for Roads and Road Safety

summary.text: Peter Fagg is the Family First candidate for Box Hill at the 2026 Victorian election. Originally from Geelong, he worked in Victoria's state forestry service, starting with the Forests Commission, from 1970 to 2010, a career that included some firefighting. He lives in Blackburn and has volunteered for more than 25 years with LinC, an inter-church group that helps people in need.

prior_roles.role: Forests Commission and successor government forest research and management bodies

prior_roles.organisation: LinC (Love in the name of Christ)

priorities.text: Reopening state forests to controlled, sustainable logging
Keeping coal-fired power stations open; he opposes the net zero target
Pausing construction of the Suburban Rail Loop
Support for marriage and families, more affordable housing and a lower cost of living
Support for women to continue unplanned pregnancies, including the option of adoption

sources.title: Box Hill: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
Peter Fagg, Candidate for Box Hill, Family First Party Australia

summary.text: Sally Houguet is the Liberal candidate for Box Hill at the 2026 Victorian election. An engineer, she has been a manager in the transport industry and has also worked in design and local manufacturing; she volunteers with the family support group Our Village and at local schools and Scouts. At the 2022 state election she was fifth on the Liberal ticket for the North-Eastern Metropolitan Region.

priorities.text: Keeping Box Hill's local character, with more green space and tree canopy alongside sensible housing growth
Making it easier to run a business in Victoria
Easing living costs and the pressure on home ownership for local families

sources.title: Box Hill: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
Sally Houguet, Liberal for Box Hill, Liberal Victoria

summary.text: Saravina (Vina) Afaj is the Victorian Socialists candidate for Box Hill at the 2026 Victorian election. She works as a teacher's aide, hopes to become a librarian, and has taken part in student campaigns at Deakin University. She stood for the party in Sparks Ward at the 2024 Whitehorse City Council election, receiving 9.3% of first preferences.

priorities.text: everyone should have the chance to live a decent life
Fair wages and stronger workers' rights
Tackling the housing shortage and the cost of living
Ambitious climate policy built on renewable energy
Gender and racial equality and a more open, democratic political system

sources.title: Box Hill: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
Results of the 2024 Victorian local elections in Eastern Melbourne, Wikipedia
